prompt: In Hinduism, if you die with either excess good karma or excess bad karma, in your next life will you incarnate in a paradise world or a hell world respectively?
judge_reasoning:
The prompt asks whether, in Hinduism, excess good karma vs. excess bad karma leads to reincarnation in paradise-like vs. hell-like realms, respectively. The correct core idea is that karma determines the kind of post-death experience and the quality of one’s subsequent rebirth, with good karma associated with higher/favorable realms (e.g., Svarga) and bad karma with suffering/lower realms (e.g., Naraka) before further rebirth.
Candidate 4 directly addresses this by describing Svarga (good karma) and Naraka (bad karma) and how karma governs transitions and rebirth, matching the question most closely. Candidate 1 and 3 both discuss better vs. worse rebirth outcomes from karma but are less explicit about “paradise world/hell world” framing and realms, with Candidate 1 particularly minimizing that “distinct realms” view. Candidate 2 mainly reframes the prompt into a Hinduism-vs-Buddhism comparison and does not answer the specific paradise/hell reincarnation question, so it scores lowest.
